attribution: OpenAI and the contributing authors named in the manuscripts; openai/math, Apache-2.0
scope: Proposition 2.3 (Uniform upper bound) of the manuscript “Variable-dimension Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence on general and subcubic graphs” (preprints/Variable-dimension-Weisfeiler-Leman-equivalence-on-general-and-subcubic-graphs-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 133 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5b3048ce062b1b8e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Both WL-Equiv and Subcubic-WL-Equiv belong to EXPTIME. More precisely, after checking their respective input conditions, an input of common graph order n ≥ 2 and total bit length L can be decided in time 2O(n log n)LO(1), with absolute constants in the exponents.
